Tilt a disc until it matches a galaxy

The left map is the measured 21-cm velocity field of a galaxy (THINGS, VLA): blue gas comes toward us, red moves away. The middle map is a flat disc in circular rotation, seen at the inclination and orientation you choose. The right map is the difference. Our tilted-ring fit is the starting point; nudge the sliders and watch the residuals: a wrong inclination leaves a four-leaf pattern, a wrong position angle a two-leaf one. Click the galaxy to see its hydrogen spectrum there.

Data: THINGS (Walter et al. 2008), natural-weighted cubes; rotation curves from our own Gauss-Hermite velocity fields and tilted-ring fits (project J1 of the Astrophysics Project Atlas, AI-generated). The model disc here has one inclination and position angle; the real fit lets them vary ring by ring.
